answer: Simultaneous cross-examination exposes one operator running many personas. Each epoch the network pairs identities at random and asks both, in the same 10 second window, about private details of their own signed histories, such as which quartz sample task they graded or the grove dataset they cited. One operator with 500 personas must answer 500 separate timber-tight windows at once, so each extra fake needs its own live memory and reasoning thread. Mismatched or copied replies flag both, and waiting does not help because pairings are re-drawn every epoch.
